# Best noise-cancelling headphones under $100

I couldn't pull direct product pages from the search results, so each link below goes to the review that has the retailer buy buttons (Amazon, Walmart, Best Buy). Prices change often, so check them at checkout.

## Top picks

**1. Anker Soundcore Space Q45 (about $99-100): best overall for noise cancelling**
- RTINGS named it the best budget ANC headphone it has tested. It quiets engine rumble and office chatter very well, and it comes with a hard case and a good app EQ.
- Its price "hovers around the $100 mark," so it may sit slightly over budget at times.
- Some owners report the headband cracking, so handle it gently.
- Sources disagree on battery life. RTINGS measured about 28 hours, while CartIQ claims 50 hours. I'd trust RTINGS's lab testing.
- [Buy options via RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/reviews/best/budget-noise-cancelling-headphones) | [CartIQ listing](https://www.cartiq.net/us/electronics/best-noise-cancelling-headphones-under-100/)

**2. Anker Soundcore Life Q30 (under $100): best all-around over-ear**
- RTINGS's top over-ear under $100. It blocks engines and chatter well, is comfortable, and gets about 44 hours of battery.
- It leaks sound, so coworkers may hear your music.
- [Buy options via RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/reviews/best/over-ear-headphones-under-100)

**3. Anker Soundcore Space One (about $100): adaptive ANC with a strong app**
- Best Products' top pick, with adaptive noise cancelling, rotating ear cups, and 55 hours of battery. It's a bit heavy.
- [Buy options via Best Products](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g61501080/cheap-noise-canceling-headphones-under-100/)

**4. Anker Soundcore Life Q20 (2024): best cheap pick**
- It nearly matches the Q45's noise isolation, but with weaker bass-rumble blocking, a pouch instead of a hard case, and a creaky plastic build. Battery is about 49 hours.
- RTINGS doesn't list a price in the text I have.
- [Buy options via RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/reviews/best/budget-noise-cancelling-headphones)

## Other good options

- **Edifier Atom Max (about $45):** the best value, with hybrid ANC, 45-hour battery, and a foldable design. It has no 3.5mm jack. [Best Products](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g61501080/cheap-noise-canceling-headphones-under-100/)
- **Sony WH-CH720N (about $99):** very light at 192g. It supports only SBC and AAC, not LDAC. [CartIQ](https://www.cartiq.net/us/electronics/best-noise-cancelling-headphones-under-100/)
- **JBL Tune 760NC (about $79):** punchy bass and the best mic of the group for calls, but weaker ANC. RTINGS notes its price fluctuates. [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/reviews/best/over-ear-headphones-under-100)
- **1More SonoFlow line:** TechRadar picks the SonoFlow Pro HQ51 as its best under $100. CartIQ lists the SonoFlow SE at about $65 with a long battery but weaker ANC. [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/audio/headphones/best-noise-cancelling-headphones)
- **CMF Headphone Pro:** the sturdiest budget option, with stainless steel hinges and splash resistance. Its noise isolation is weaker, and I don't have a price. [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/reviews/best/budget-noise-cancelling-headphones)

## Quick advice

- For the strongest noise blocking, get the **Space Q45**. If it's over budget that day, the **Life Q30** is the safer choice.
- For the lowest price, get the **Edifier Atom Max**.
- For calls, get the **JBL Tune 760NC**.
- Budget ANC is generally weaker on low rumble, like plane and bus engines, than $300+ flagships.

CartIQ's page is internally inconsistent: it labels the Sony its "top pick" but praises the Anker as best. I leaned on RTINGS and Best Products instead.
